key_insight: Most surveyed eSanjeevani hub clinicians intended to keep using its AI-enabled decision support, but intention was lower when diagnostic suggestions were inappropriate or absent.
clinical_relevance: Provider feedback highlights the importance of relevant diagnostic suggestions and usable symptom capture in telemedicine workflows, without establishing diagnostic accuracy or patient benefit.
method: Analyzed a July 2025 program feedback survey of 190 hub clinicians and 662 spoke providers.
Assessed role-specific experiences with symptom summaries, AI suggestions and usability.
Compared within-role acceptance using absolute differences and 95% confidence intervals; analyzed short comments.
evidence_signal: Among hub respondents, 85.3% intended continued use; intention was 23.2 percentage points lower with mostly inappropriate suggestions and 25.7 points lower with mostly absent suggestions than with matched or appropriate suggestions.
watch_item: Low survey response rates—21.4% for hub and 19.3% for spoke providers—may limit representativeness; these self-reports do not establish clinical effectiveness.
paper_title: Provider Experiences with AI Clinical Decision Support in eSanjeevani
